slides.title: Get started
slides.html:
Proof menu: four diagrams, four routes (vertical angles, SAS, ASA, SSS). Teams match each diagram to its fastest route before proving anything.

  • I can choose the shortest valid route: a direct angle theorem when it is enough, and SSS, SAS or ASA only when it is needed.
  • I can reject a proof whose premises are SSA.

Diagonal of a quadrilateral, by SSS (original).

Triangle ABC ≅ triangle CDA.SSS. A matches C, B matches D, C matches A.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
Vertical angles only (original).

Read the worked steps
StepReason
Lines AB and CD cross at O. Angle AOC = (3x + 4) degrees and angle BOD = (5x - 20) degrees.Given.
3x + 4 = 5x - 20.Vertical angles are equal.
x = 12, so both angles are 40 degrees.Solve and substitute.
No triangles needed.Pick the shortest route.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
The kite.

Read the worked steps
StepReason
Convex quadrilateral ABCD has AB = AD and CB = CD.Given. Convex matters: it keeps diagonal AC inside angle BAD.
AC = AC.A segment equals itself.
Triangle ABC ≅ triangle ADC.SSS.
Angle BAC = angle DAC and angle BCA = angle DCA.CPCTC. Because ABCD is convex, AC is inside both angles, so AC bisects them. Saying the diagonals are perpendicular would need more proof.

steps.step: Convex quadrilateral ABCD has AB = AD and CB = CD.
steps.reason: Given. Convex matters: it keeps diagonal AC inside angle BAD.

steps.step: Angle BAC = angle DAC and angle BCA = angle DCA.
steps.reason: CPCTC. Because ABCD is convex, AC is inside both angles, so AC bisects them. Saying the diagonals are perpendicular would need more proof.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
Jordan tries to prove two triangles congruent just to find an angle that vertical angles already give.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Find and fix the error

Jordan draws triangles AOC and BOD and tries to prove them congruent to find the angle in Worked example 2. That cannot work: the two triangles are clearly different sizes. No triangles are needed. Angles AOC and BOD are vertical angles, so they are equal in one step. Check for a direct angle fact first.

Reveal solution

Reveal second check

40 + 140 = 180.

slides.title: Practice 4
slides.html:
In the convex kite, AB = 2x + 1 and AD = 11. Find x.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

The equal sides give 2x + 1 = 11, so x = 5.

Reveal second check

Plug in: 2(5) + 1 = 11.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html:
Given AB = CD and BC = DA in quadrilateral ABCD. Which two triangles and which test show angle B = angle D?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Triangles ABC and CDA share AC; with AB = CD and BC = DA they are congruent by SSS, so angle B = angle D by CPCTC.

Reveal second check

Name the givens and the theorem or definition used.
